AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL

  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206

 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at http://www.glendaleca.gov/government/agendas-minutes . If you
 have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City
 Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who wish
 to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City Clerk’s
 office at 818-548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify the language
 for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not required and
 persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  ORGANIZATION MEETING
  MARCH 31, 2020

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale City Council meeting will be available to the public
electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6.

4. NEW BUSINESS
  a. City Clerk, re: Declaring the Result of the General Municipal Election of
  March 3, 2020

  Presenting:
  Rita Buchanan, City Resource Specialist

  1. Resolution 20-37 Reciting the Fact of the General Municipal Election Held on
  Tuesday, March 3, 2020 and declaring the Results and Such Other Matters as
  Provided by Law
  Moved:  Agajanian  Seconded:  Quintero
  Vote as Follows
  Ayes:  Agajanian, Devine, Gharpetian, Quintero, Najarian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

5. COMMENTS BY OUTGOING COUNCILMEMBERS
  Council Member Gharpetian thanked his family, friends, and campaign team for standing
  beside him all this time and for their support. Although the results were not in his favor, he
  thanked the residents for their vote of confidence. It has been his honor serving the City of
  Glendale, for being a Mayor during his term, for attending many community organizations,
  and address citizens’ concerns. Glendale has been their home for many years and is proud
  to raise their family in this city. Every decision he had made on the dais was for the best
  interest of the city. He was proud to say that he was never been to behold to any special-
  interest group or group of people. He took full responsibility regarding the results of the
  election and stated that this election was heavily influenced by many outside special-interest
  groups. He hoped that this trend will not continue. He thanked his colleagues for their
  leadership and professionalism. He thanked the City Management, City staff and
  departments for the great services they provided and helped improved the quality of life of
  our residents. During these tough times due to COVID-19 pandemic, he thanked the Fire
  and Police Department for their dedication and commitment to keep our city safe. Lastly, he
  leaves the Council with utmost pride and dignity and has served his community well. He
  looked forward being involved in a different capacity and sent his congratulations to the
  newly-elected council members.

  Council Member Quintero thanked Council for the appointment and for the vote of
  confidence. He looked forward to the new councilmembers. He commended City Manager
  Yasmin Beers, Asst. City Manager Rouibik Golanian, and all the current department heads.
  He stated that this has been the best team he had worked with in all these years being
  involved with the City. He thanked the essential departments for their hard work during the
  pandemic. In the several months he has served, he is happy where the city is heading to
  and what the Council has accomplished during his tenure – GWP Renewable Component,
  Accessory Dwelling Units, Short-term Rental Issues, Acquisition of two large properties, and
  the Lobbyist Registration Ordinance. In closing, he is confident the City of Glendale will get
  through this crisis.

  03 31 20
  CC
 6. RECESS

  NEW COUNCIL

1. OATH OF OFFICE TO NEWLY ELECTED CITY OFFICERS: Senator Anthony
  Portantino COUNCIL MEMBERS

  Newly-Elected Councilmembers Paula Devine, Ardy Kassakhian, and Daniel Brotman
2. NEW COUNCIL IS SEATED

3. COMMENTS BY NEWLY-ELECTED COUNCILMEMBERS
  Council Member Devine thanked Mayor Najarian and Council Member Agajanian. She
  looked forward working together with them for the next four years. She sent her
  congratulatory remarks to her new colleagues Kassakhian and Brotman and looked forward
  to working together and sharing new ideas which will ensure the city will run efficiently and
  remain sustainable so residents can continue to enjoy the excellent quality of life and
  receive the services they deserve. She thanked the residents of Glendale for the support
  and confidence for reelecting her. She thanked her campaign staff, endorsers, and
  volunteers. She thanked her husband for his enduring support. Important decisions are
  made on the dais that she takes very seriously and the input of the residences is part of the
  decisions she makes. She will continue to listen to residents and she will be their voice. Her
  vision for the next four years is simple: to make residents’ lives better, continue to protect
  the integrity of the neighborhoods, continue to make decisions based on standards and
  codes in order to protect historical resources, monitor the progress of the Grayson Power
  Plant, continue to pursue the banning of using plastic utensils in establishments, continue to
  pursue the food recovery program, and improve traffic congestion and safety. Other major
  goals Ms. Devine want to accomplish for the next four years are: provide more affordable
  housing, groundbreaking of the Armenian-American Museum, complete and redesign of
  Artsakh Avenue, create more vigor and active Central Park, implement Urban Arts Plan,
  support our Iconic Theatre, and support technology sector and all small and large
  businesses. Finally, she commended city staff and the City Manager for making sure that
  the city runs safely, efficiently, and smoothly during the COVID-19 pandemic. She is proud
  of the Council for passing Resolutions to ensure the help and economic welfare of our
  residents. She acknowledged the front-liners for risking their lives to sustain and stop the
  spread of the virus. In order to beat the virus, residents should follow the Government’s
  guideline of social-distancing and staying home. As this crisis passes, which it will, she
  stated that our great city will remain standing and be better than before.

  Council Member Kassakhian congratulated the new councilmembers and thanked the
  citizens who were watching live on TV or online. He hoped that everyone is safe and healthy
  during this pandemic. Every two years, the voters have exercised their rights to vote in the
  polls or at home, for individuals who they believe will represent them in Council. He thanked
  outgoing Councilmembers Gharpetian and Quintero for their service to Glendale. He
  congratulated School Board Members Freemon and Nahabedian, he looked forward to
  working with them and building relationship. He is ready to support the schools, students,
  administrators, and the board to ensure that the public educations have the resources to
  succeed. He also congratulated College Trustees Rabinov and Benlian. He looked forward
  to working with them as well. Glendale’s public schools and College are one of the reasons
  why our city sparkles so brightly. When our public institutions succeed, we all succeed. He
  also thanked the City Clerk’s Staff for their hard work and dedication over the last decade
  and a half as their Glendale City Clerk. He’s had the privilege of working with some of the
  best professionals in the field and despite the pressure they have continuously delivered to
  03 31 20
  CC
 the citizens of Glendale exceptional service with integrity. Glendale should be proud of the
people in that office and their commitment of preserving the democracy of our city. He
thanked his parents and his family without whom he would not be who he was today. He
thanked his spouse Courtney and his 5-year old son, that despite his years of professional
experience and study, he still has a lot to learn. His family is the most important part of his
life and they are a constant reminder of how blessed he was and also one of the reasons
why he made this commitment to serve. His agenda has not changed: absolute
transparency, greater accountability, fiscal responsibility, environmental sustainability, and
ensure the safety and security of our neighborhoods. By celebrating our diverse culture,
supporting the arts programs, and working together to help our local businesses, this will
help us guide through the dark times. Besides the weekly Council Meetings, he will also
meet with the homeowners, renters, and business owners on a regular basis. He will
continue to be accessible as social-distancing will allow and will continue to listen to
residents before making any decisions. He thanked the voters for their support and trust and
fully acknowledged he is taking this seat at a difficult time. The journey for the next four
years would be rocky; he promised not only his best efforts but also promised the truth.

Council Member Brotman congratulated Ms. Devine and Mr. Kassakhian on their
campaigns. He said he looked forward to working with Council and City Staff despite having
“butted heads” with some in the past. He stressed that, despite past differences, he
recognizes that City Staff are good people who work hard and always do what they think is
best for the City. Mr. Brotman explained that he learned a huge amount about the City
during the campaign, walking virtually every neighborhood and knocking on thousands of
doors. Despite the normal complaining, Glendale really has a lot going for it. It has a deep
pool of talented people that care and want to contribute. It is a well-functioning and safe city,
and while just minutes from the center of one of the most dynamic metro areas in the world,
is able to maintain a certain “small town” feel. It enjoys amazing natural abundance–parks
and open space, and neighborhoods full of historic character. It is also rich in diversity—
historically a driver of creativity and innovation. Still, it can do a lot more if it rejects business
as usual thinking.Glendale has made good progress on sustainability, especially renewable
energy, but these are still baby steps. Mr. Brotman said we need to get to 100% clean
energy as soon as possible. But to meet the State’s greenhouse gas reduction goals, we
need to also focus on buildings and transportation. He called for an ordinance to ensure all
new construction is 100% electric and for incentives to retrofit existing buildings. He said
that we can reduce car-miles traveled by making alternative modes of transportation safer
and more convenient, and that doing so will also help address issues of pedestrian safety,
air pollution, and traffic. He called for expediting the Citywide Pedestrian Plan. He also
talked about waste issues, including closing the Scholl Canyon dump and reducing single-
use plastics. He is encouraged by plans to set up an Office of Sustainability but wants to be
sure it is fully empowered to develop policy and hold us accountable. Lastly, he stressed the
need to work on climate adaptation and disaster preparedness as the city gets hotter, drier
and more fire-prone. Mr. Brotman also discussed housing. He said the State is bearing
down on us to build more housing, especially affordable housing. While we must insist that
the people of Glendale—not Sacramento—get to decide where and how this housing gets
developed, more density is inevitable. The question is how we manage it. He reiterated his
vision of a walkable and transit-connected downtown with great eateries, culture, and art,
coupled with dogged preservation of our unique single-family neighborhoods. He also
discussed the need to make government more representative and responsive. He called for
taking a hard look at Council districts, campaign finance, the operation of our Boards and
Commissions, and our general attitude toward public input. Mr. Brotman asked the public to
take the COVID-19 pandemic seriously and to stay home. He warned that the economic
impact will be severe and that we will need to get creative to prevent a wave of evictions and
small business failures. However, some good will come out of this too because it will shake
  03 31 20

   us out of old ways of doing things, demonstrate our adaptability, and bring the community
  closer together. He said he was excited to contribute to putting the pieces back together in a
  way to make Glendale even better. He ended by thanking everyone who voted in the
  election, whether for him or not, because civic engagement really matters.

4. ADJOURNMENT – 8:51 p.m.
  Moved:  Agajanian  Seconded:  Devine

  Mayor of the City of Glendale

  City Clerk of the City of Glendale
